summary: States that the IPv6 address space will be managed by the IANA for the good of the Internet community, with advice from the IAB and IESG, by delegation to the regional registries. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC states that IANA manages IPv6 address space with advice from the IAB and IESG. IANA delegates specific allocations to regional and other registries, from which organizations can obtain addresses directly or through a service provider.

subtitle: A proposed management and delegation structure for IPv6 address space.

tldr.problem: IPv6 address space needed a management structure for delegation and allocation on behalf of the Internet community.
tldr.mechanism: The memo assigns management responsibility to IANA, with advice from the IAB and IESG, and delegates specific allocations to regional and other registries.
tldr.outcome: It sets out principles for allocation, delegation, revocation, registry fees, and a plan for initial IPv6 allocation.

today: RFC 1881 is Informational and sets out a proposed structure for managing IPv6 address allocation. It does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: Who Manages IPv6 Address Space
sections.content:
The memo says IPv6 address space must be managed for the good of the Internet community and that good management requires some central authority over delegation and allocation. It identifies IANA as the appropriate entity, with advice from the Internet Architecture Board and Internet Engineering Steering Group.

IANA delegates specific allocations to regional and other registries, which in turn allocate addresses to network service providers and other subregional registries. Individuals and organizations may obtain allocations through a registry or service provider.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA oversees the address space and delegates allocation work to registries. Organizations can obtain an allocation from a registry or through a service provider.

sections.title: Delegation and Fees
sections.content:
The RFC says an IANA delegation to a registry is not irrevocable. If IANA judges that a registry has seriously mishandled its delegated space, it may revoke the delegation after notice and consideration of operational effects. It says IANA will try not to revoke addresses in active use unless there are overwhelming technical reasons.

Any revenue related to the address space should cover registry expenses only; the address space itself is not charged for, though cost-recovery fees may apply. The memo also says monopoly control and predatory practices must be avoided.
sections.plainLanguage: A registry can lose its delegated authority if it seriously mishandles the space. Fees may cover registry costs, but the address space itself is not sold.

sections.title: Initial Allocation and Appeals
sections.content: The RFC says IANA will develop a plan for initial IPv6 allocation, including automatic allocation to holders of IPv4 addresses. It also says IANA will develop mediation and appeals procedures for delegation and revocation.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo calls for an initial allocation plan and procedures to handle disputes about delegation and revocation.

sections.title: Status of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1881 provides information to the Internet community and does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This document describes allocation-management principles. It does not define an Internet standard.
